column2: A day at Marche begins with a greeting. Students nod politely to classmates in the corridor and are careful even with the clink of a teacup. At this faculty, whose symbol is the white lily, refinement is not an affectation but something that settles into the body.

Their major is Protocol. Drawing on court etiquette, they learn who sits where, in what order to make introductions, and how to refuse an awkward guest without losing face. Magic is held to the same standard: precision over power, elegance over flash.

They accept subjugation as a necessary duty but will not take part in adventures for the sake of war stories. A Marche subjugation plan tends to list every backup route and retreat signal. As members of the Legacy Society, they believe old methods exist for a reason and are cautious about the new.
If you pour care into every greeting and every teacup, Marche suits you well.

The Rossier lounge is liveliest in the evening. News passes around about which estate had a bad harvest this year or which family broke off an engagement, and deals are sometimes struck before the teacups are empty. Students of this faculty, whose symbol is the fox, are astonishingly good at reading people and situations.

Their major is Diplomacy. At the negotiating table they learn to tilt a situation in their favor rather than clash head-on, and to choose the right means for each end. Their competitive streak makes them sharpen one another.

They see subjugation as a chance to raise their own name and their family's. Instead of overpowering a foe, they find its weak points and set the board to win. As members of the Pioneer Society, they do not linger on stale tricks and keep testing new rhetoric and formations.
If reading people and situations delights you, Rossier suits you well.

At Varche, anywhere can be a stage. A corridor or a dining hall becomes a small theater in moments: someone sings, someone stages a scene with magic, and now and then someone confesses their love. At this faculty, whose symbol is the rose, showing yourself off is a talent in its own right.

Their major is Rhetoric. They learn to change a room's mood with a single word, to breathe so that feeling carries, and to stand before an audience. They value personal charm over family name and prefer showy magic and attacks that command attention.

Subjugation is the best stage on which to prove their ability. The more eyes watching, the stronger they get, and they are more eager than anyone about romance and socializing. As members of the Pioneer Society, they always welcome new staging and new spell combinations.
If shining before an audience delights you, Varche suits you well.

A day at Tonica begins with the sound of training in the early morning. Nobody orders it; it has simply become custom that whoever arrives first lights the lamps. The morning greeting here is the clack of wooden swords and a hearty shout. The faculty is rough but holds no grudges, and its symbol, the lion, reflects how highly it prizes loyalty.

Their major is Martial Arts. They hone bladed weapons and bodywork, and use magic only to support the weapon. This is a Legacy Society faculty that treasures old things such as sword schools and knightly oaths.

They consider a gate an evil that must be struck down. They put honor before profit and step forward into danger before the weak do. Their fighting style differs from Bronte's, so the two often clash.
If you are not afraid to stand at the front, Tonica suits you well.

At Bronte, the one who just tries it earns respect. Its students are people who are already on site while others are still writing the third page of the plan. At this faculty, whose symbol is lightning, failure is not shameful but a ticket to the next challenge. When lightning strikes, students crowd to the windows.

Their major is Tactics. They learn to break formations and charge through, to deliver a short, hard blow, and to fight where a split-second decision decides the outcome. Bold and direct, they prefer explosive abilities. While others calculate, this faculty takes the first step.

Subjugation is the event they look forward to most. They believe a challenge is worth more the more dangerous it is, and count the days until they face a powerful boss. As members of the Pioneer Society, they are wide open to new techniques and tactics. Opening a breach at the very front of the line is their pride.
If you feel that time spent hesitating is the most wasted, Bronte suits you well.

At Castel, everyone stands at the front at least once. Looking down on the whole field from a high place and giving orders is daily practice. At this faculty, whose symbol is the citadel tower, those who see leading a group as their duty gather, and their sense of responsibility and pride is just as strong.

Their major is Command. They learn to form up, to work as a team, tactics that value stability and endurance, and even the judgment to decide on a retreat. They prefer abilities suited to command and cooperation.

They believe subjugation is the duty of the strong to protect the weak. Taking the vanguard and ordering a withdrawal are both responsibilities, so they are quick to call a retreat. Charge-minded faculties tease them as cowards, but Castel counts bringing everyone home as victory.
If you are willing to bear the responsibility of leading others, Castel suits you well.

At Erva, "But why?" is more common than hello. Answers do not shorten the questions; every question solved gives rise to two more. At this faculty, whose symbol is the key, people gather who cannot see a closed door without trying to open it. Their curiosity borders on obsession, and they dig into any unrevealed truth to the end.

Their major is History. Centered on deciphering ancient texts and exploring ruins, they question even restricted records and knowledge deemed taboo. They prefer magic and ancient technology, and are keen to apply whatever they newly discover.

Their reason for entering a gate is also research. They go on subjugations to find out why gates appear, what laws govern their interiors, and what the bosses really are. As members of the Pioneer Society, they organize and share what they uncover.
If you are someone who cannot stop asking questions, Erva suits you well.

At Levant, it is the person in a hurry who stands out. This faculty, centered on elven culture and nature magic, is unhurried and aloof, and famed for a bond in which everyone stands by whoever is in trouble. True to its symbol, the deer, even its voices and footsteps are quiet. They sense one another's hearts without raising their voices.
Their major is Pharmacology. They learn old knowledge of herbs and spirits, archery, and nature magic. They also learn to care for people and nature together, as one tends a garden.

They see a gate not as something to conquer but as something whose ecology and environment must be understood. Even on subjugation they do not hurry, reading the flow of the place first. Even within the Legacy Society they are the quietest faculty, and they carry on old records with care. Listening to the voices of nature and spirits is the first step of a subjugation.
If you wish to carry on what has been quietly guarded for ages, Levant suits you well.

At Volter, something is always blowing up somewhere. Fortunately most of it is small, and students wear their scorched uniforms like medals. This faculty, whose symbol is the flame, puts curiosity before safety, so fire-suppression magic is the first basic skill everyone learns. The lab lights are almost never out.

Their major is Alchemy. They transform existing knowledge and magic, experimenting to create new uses. They would rather test things themselves than follow fixed principles and customs, and they record every failed experiment.

The experiments continue on subjugation too. They sometimes get scolded by other faculties for testing odd combinations "to check the boss's pattern," but when everyone is stuck, it is Volter that finds a breakthrough by an absurd method. It is a leading faculty of the Pioneer Society.
If you believe research that isn't fun isn't research, Volter suits you well.

Bellois mornings start with checking prices. Glancing at mana stones, herbs, iron, even this week's cafeteria menu, they decide what to buy and sell today. At this faculty, whose symbol is the coin, everything has a price, and whoever knows the price stays a step ahead.

Their major is Trade. They learn commerce and the use of magic tools, and choose magic and bodywork alike by practicality and efficiency. Realistic and quick at figures, they calculate exactly what comes back to them.

Subjugation is a business. They first calculate reward, spoils, fame and risk, and set personnel and equipment to match. They would rather cut back when the loss is large, but since mandatory subjugations cannot be avoided, they then squeeze out maximum efficiency at minimum cost. As befits the Pioneer Society, they are eager for new customers and new technology.
If you are quick with numbers and see reality clearly, Bellois suits you well.

At Janus, holding your tongue is a virtue. Students in the corridor pass with only a quiet nod, and no one can tell what they know. This faculty, whose symbol is the crow, gathers people with sharp observation who can keep secrets.

Their major is Intelligence. They learn to gather and analyze information, sift fact from rumor, and grasp a situation. Because they speak little, each word carries weight, and they are raised to know how much of what they have heard may be told.

On subjugations they spend the most time on advance investigation. They collect the boss's past records, internal layout and appearance patterns, and sometimes hand needed information to other faculties. As the Legacy Society, they carry on the old intelligence network and rules, and set strict lines around the secrets to be kept.
If listening comes easier to you than speaking, Janus suits you well.

Students at Orden know one another's circumstances well. When classes get busy, study groups form without a word, and on the desk of a classmate absent through illness, lecture notes appear before long. At this faculty, whose symbol is the ear of wheat, order is not rules but consideration for one another. The warmth hidden in that order is the faculty's real charm.

Their major is Logistics. They learn supply and provisions, personnel placement, and community management. They value discipline, stability and practical results, and put the safety and prosperity of the whole community before any one person's glory. They each try to be first to take on grunt work such as serving meals and sorting supplies.

On subjugation too, Orden is responsible for the rear. They check food, medicine and routes first, and move only after securing the way for everyone to return. They are one pillar of the Legacy Society, which regards responsibility for tradition and community as a noble's most important duty.
If you find fulfillment in taking responsibility for a community, Orden suits you well.

The Office is where the lights come on earliest and go out latest in the Academy. The facade with its thick columns and the deliberately high stone steps are said to mean "catch your breath before you climb." Most visitors come about paperwork, so it is usually as quiet as a government office.

The Office runs the whole Academy, separate from the twelve faculties. Academy rules, admission and graduation, review of faculty transfers, and staff matters are all handled here. The Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Head of the Office, Head of the Infirmary and Dorm Warden work here, and the one instructor assigned to each faculty also belongs to the Office.

The Office is at the center of subjugation as well. When a gate appears it rates the grade and posts the commission, then reviews and approves the parties students form. Students must go on a subjugation at least once a month during term, and for the Grand Subjugations of June and November the Office itself picks the gates and sends out the whole student body.
Keeping the balance so that no single nation's influence grows too large is also the Office's work.
Today's learning averts tomorrow's disaster.
To observe courtesy is to give your whole heart.
Whoever reads the board has already won.
Shining needs no one else's permission.
Those who retreat leave no name behind.
Nothing is proven on the safe road.
One acts for all.
Hidden truths belong to those who dig.
We have watched for so long that we never hurry.
There are no failed experiments, only new ones.
There is no risk that cannot be priced.
The one who knows keeps silent; the one who speaks never knows it all.
Ear by ear, a vast wheat field is made.

Administration

The administrative body that runs the whole Academy and oversees academy rules and admission and graduation. The five staff members (Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Head of the Office, Head of the Infirmary, Dorm Warden) and the instructors of the twelve faculties belong to it. It also handles posting and approval of subjugation commissions.
Basic Setting
A classic medieval fantasy of swords and magic. The Academy is an international academy founded jointly by several nations, and those who are not nobles may enter with a letter of recommendation.
Why the Academy Runs

It was founded jointly by several nations so that they could respond together to the gates and no single nation could monopolize subjugation. Operating costs are shared among the participating nations, and the Academy runs on the patronage of six nations.
Admission and Cohorts

Only adults aged twenty or older may enter, and the course lasts three years. A new cohort is recruited every three years; a cohort enters at the same time, studies together, and graduates at the same time. In principle, all characters are classmates of the same cohort.
A Place Without Seniors and Juniors
There are no senior-junior relationships among students. No one acts on the assumption of year differences, and they call one another by name or as "classmate."
Admission Screening
The Sanctuary of Oridia and the Republic of Northeia have no noble system. People from those two nations enter through each nation's admission screening and are treated as equals to nobles.
Choosing a Faculty

New students have already chosen a faculty before admission. At the entrance ceremony, when they receive the jeweled brooch in the faculty's color, they formally become a member of that faculty. Once chosen it cannot be changed, but with just cause a change can be made through the Office.
What Is a Gate
Appearance
Appears intermittently in the form of a dimensional door. The conditions for its appearance are unknown.
Grades
Divided into grades F, E, D, C, B, A, S, SS and EX. The higher the grade, the greater the base merit.
Boss and Interior
Every gate has a boss, and its interior environment is formed to suit that boss.
Danger of Neglect
If neglected, the boss comes out and harms humanity, so it must be subjugated before then.
Subjugation and Closure
When the boss dies, the environment and creatures inside immediately lose their aggression, and the gate closes after about 24 hours.
The Highest Honor
Gate subjugation is the highest honor.
Subjugation Operations
1. Posting the Commission

When a gate appears, the Office rates its grade, and the Head of the Office posts a commission on the notice board in front of the Office. The commission lists the grade, location, base merit and subjugation deadline.
2. Applying as a Party
Students who wish to subjugate form a party and apply to the Office. A party has at least two members and is formed freely regardless of faculty. One of the members serves as leader.
3. Approval

The Office reviews the members' Circles and composition and approves the application, rejecting grades that are too ambitious. For SS grade and above an instructor accompanies the party, but a student remains leader.
4. Expedition
Gate locations range from near Northeia to other nations, and parties set out by carriage. The length of the expedition runs from a single day to several days depending on grade and distance.
5. Missed Deadline
A gate not subjugated by its deadline lets its boss out to cause damage. In that case the Office leads an emergency subjugation.
6. Report
When the subjugation ends, members report the result to the Office, and merit is reflected immediately.
Once-a-Month Duty
Students must take part in a subjugation at least once a month during term. Those who miss it receive remedial guidance from the Office. During breaks there is no duty and participation is voluntary.
Gates That Never Rest
Gates appear even during breaks and events, and subjugation continues.
Merit System
What Is Merit

Points by which the Academy honors students' achievements and motivates them. Valid only within the Academy and without effect in international society or in any nation. Faculty merit and personal merit are tallied separately.
Faculty Merit
When a subjugation succeeds, any faculty with even one member in the party receives the full base merit. It is not divided, and a faculty with several participants still receives it only once.
Personal Merit
Every participating student receives the full base merit as personal merit, regardless of faculty.
Leader Bonus
The party leader receives an additional 50% of the base merit. It applies to both the leader's own personal merit and the merit of the leader's faculty.
Party Composition
Parties may be formed freely regardless of faculty. There is no disadvantage to a single-faculty or mixed party.
Failed Subjugation
If a subjugation fails, no merit is awarded.
Faculty Rankings and Treatment
Tallying Rankings

Faculty merit accumulates by semester and resets on settlement day. Rankings are tallied in real time during the semester, and treatment applies immediately according to the current ranking. When all merit is equal at the start of a semester, no distinctions are made.
Top 3 Faculties · Expedition
They travel in a dedicated carriage bearing the faculty crest, use dedicated tents and insulating magic tools, and borrow high-grade equipment from the armory.
Top 3 Faculties · Banquets
They use the VIP rooms, terrace and garden of the Banquet Wing without reservation, and sit in the seats of honor at balls.
Bottom 3 Faculties · Expedition
They travel in the cargo bed of a freight wagon or on foot, use cramped, drafty, worn communal tents, and may borrow only worn equipment from the armory.
Bottom 3 Faculties · Banquets

They may use only the Grand and Small Banquet Halls and sit in the lowest seats at balls. They cannot enter the VIP rooms, terrace or garden, but may enter if invited as a companion by a student of a top-3 faculty.
Middle 6 Faculties
Neither benefit nor penalty. Treatment differs only for the top 3 and bottom 3 faculties.
First Place, Individual

Personal merit accumulates over the semester separately from faculty rankings. The student with the highest personal merit in the whole Academy each semester may use the Banquet Wing garden by themselves for that semester.
